Fifth release candidate of SANKHYA, the LP / MILP / convex QP solver written from scratch for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement SIH26119 (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd). 135 commits on `main` since v1.0.0-rc2, these notes included.

v1.0.0-rc3 and v1.0.0-rc4 were tags without a release: their archives built, but neither tagged commit carried release notes, so the release workflow drafted no release for them. This candidate is the first release since rc2, and the changes below are counted from rc2.

## Download

| asset | for |
|---|---|
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cpu.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64, glibc 2.35 or later |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA driver; the CUDA runtime is linked in |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-windows-x64-cpu.zip` | Windows 10 / 11 x64 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-windows-x64-cuda.zip` | Windows 10 / 11 x64 with an NVIDIA driver; the CUDA runtime and cuSPARSE DLLs are beside the binary |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl` | `pip install` on Linux x86-64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl` | `pip install` on Windows x64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-image.tar.gz` | the container image, for `docker load` offline |
| `SHA256SUMS` | over every archive and wheel |

No compiler is needed. Unpack an archive, then from the unpacked directory:

    build/sankhya version
    build/sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --write-sol blend.sol
    python3 tools/verify_solution.py demo/crude_blend.mps blend.sol
    demo/finale.sh                     # Windows: demo\finale.cmd

**Python wheels.** The bindings are ctypes over the C API, so one wheel per platform carries the library and the CLI and serves every CPython from 3.9 to 3.13; CI installs each into a clean venv of each of those five versions and solves and verifies the demo there before the draft is made. Nothing is on PyPI; install straight from this release:

    pip install https://github.com/thegoodengineers/SANKHYA/releases/download/v1.0.0-rc5/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl
    # Windows: .../v1.0.0-rc5/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl
    python -c "import sankhya; print(sankhya.Model.read('demo/crude_blend.mps').solve().objective)"

Container (CUDA build, the verifier and the demo models):

    docker pull ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0-rc5
    docker run --rm --gpus all ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0-rc5 sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --gpu

Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`. Each archive's `MANIFEST.txt` records the commit, compiler and CUDA toolkit it was built with and the libraries it links; CI fails the packaging if any of them is an optimization solver.

The Windows CUDA archive was new in rc2. The tree now builds under MSVC, the host compiler nvcc requires on Windows, and the archive is built with the CUDA 12.6 toolkit on a `windows-2022` runner, compiled without a card; the CUDA runtime, cuSPARSE and MSVC runtime DLLs ship beside the binary. CI unpacks it on a runner with no compiler and no card: `--gpu` warns and solves on the CPU, and the verifier accepts the answer. Its kernels have not yet been run on a Windows machine with a card.

## What changed since rc2

**LP.** On the full Netlib set the optimal answer is certified, within relative 1e-6 of a bound the verifier re-derives in exact arithmetic, on 93 of 94 LPs with `certified_gap_seconds=120` (#1137); greenbea, greenbeb and pilot87 gained safe bounds on the way (#1017, #1119). Presolve substitutes columns out of equality rows, chains included (#1114), and `presolve_substitution` is on by default after its same-job A/B (#1125). The Forrest-Tomlin update keeps its U in contiguous files, scans alpha's support and installs the spike the FTRAN kept (#1043, #1077, #1101); hyper-sparse FTRAN and BTRAN run over it (#1134). The dual ratio test and pricing do less work per pivot (#1018, #1020, #1031). The crossover's pivot budget is per row and column, so where it gives up does not depend on the machine (#1080). Matrices built from model data keep coefficients below the fill threshold (#1107), and the refinement after the pivot rounds has a dual phase and its own budget (#1128). The supernodal factorization runs on several threads (#1035).

**MILP.** Lifted flow cover cuts (#1131). The parity heuristic is on by default after its tier-1 A/B (#1022), and Feasibility Jump is on by default as #931 intended (#1024) and stops when it stalls (#1044). The root cut loop moves rows slack at its last LP to the cut pool (#1143). Restarts count the fixings that learned conflicts imply (#1057). Measured and left off: RINS (#1083), the tailed root cut loop (#1142), propagation dive and local branching (#999).

**QP.** The QP interior point's stall hand-off and active-set finish are on by default after their A/B (#1016); the finish is rank-revealing (#1029) and answers to the solve's clock (#1034); each Newton step is refined against the unregularized KKT matrix (#1010). Reference errata for `huestis` and `hues-mod` sit beside their exact optima (#1078).

**Conic.** A second-order cone interior point solves SOCP and convex quadratically constrained QPs (#1061, #1121), and MIQCP by depth-first branch and bound over it (#1133).

**Decomposition.** Dantzig-Wolfe over linking rows, behind `decomposition=dantzig-wolfe` (#1068). Benders forecasts its work from the structure and solves monolithically at once when decomposition cannot pay (#1066).

**Warm start.** Rows and columns can be removed through the C API and Python, and a warm re-solve after any structural edit maps the earlier basis by name (#1117). `sankhya_solve_from` carries the PDHG iterate (#1037).

**Build and tooling.** A column loop forks an OpenMP team only when its work exceeds `omp_min_work`, and `threads` is applied on the global and nonlinear paths (#1103). The tree builds and passes its tests under GCC 15 on ubuntu-26.04 (#1109); the Linux runners are pinned to ubuntu-24.04 (#1099). CUDA units pass `/utf-8` to the MSVC host compiler (#1148). The C API option setters apply the registry's checks (#1090). The MPS, LP and `.sol` readers and the verifier were tightened on names, numbers and bounds (#1087 to #1097). Benchmarks run as dispatched suites on GitHub-hosted runners, both arms of an option A/B in one job (#1045, #1085, #1105). The Apache-2.0 licence text is in the tree (#1002).

## Measured on main, from the CSVs in bench/results/

- Netlib certified gaps, all 94 LPs at `81b812c` with `certified_gap_seconds=120` (`certified-gap-netlib-full-81b812c.csv`, `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` section 1c.2): **93 of 94** certified to 1e-6 relative (worst 5.1e-08); pilot87 has a finite but looser bound (5.36e-06); the stated bound is re-derived exactly by the verifier on 94 of 94. Without that setting the count is 92 of 94 (`certified-gap-netlib-full-92ef682.csv`).
- Presolve substitution, off against on in one job at `b4bfb56` (`option-ab-{netlib,kennington,refinery}-substitution-off-b4bfb56.csv`, cited in `docs/PROVENANCE.md`): 94 of 94, 16 of 16 and 18 of 18 verified in both arms over Netlib, Kennington and the refinery LPs; shifted-geomean iterations -11%, -7% and -9% with it on.
- Maros-Meszaros head-to-head, 138 QPs at 60 s, one thread, every solver graded the same (`head-to-head-maros-meszaros-d0eb672.csv`, section 4a.3): **PIQP is ahead**, 130 matched and 135 verified at a shifted geometric mean of 1.905 s; SANKHYA 117 matched and 119 verified at 4.066 s; Clarabel and SCS 105 matched each, OSQP 61.
- Convex QCQP from QPLIB, 13 instances at 300 s (`qplib-qcqp-8a463fb.csv`, section "The convex QCQPs"): the conic engine ends `optimal` on 13 of 13 but **only 1 of 13 passes**, that is matches within 1e-6 and is accepted by the verifier; on the other 12 the verifier rejects dual feasibility (worst 1.1e-07 to 3.1e-05). `nonconvex=global` passes 0 of 13, all time limits.
- Benders on the refinery ladder at `10ed998` (`decomposition-10ed998.csv`, section 1f.6): 12 of 12 verified at the exact optimum; the forecast gave up on 8 of 9 decomposed runs and solved monolithically, and the 1 that ran Benders was not faster. Dantzig-Wolfe (`dantzig-wolfe-1bcb251.csv`): all 9 decomposed runs reach the monolithic optimum and verify, and every one is slower than the monolithic solve.
- Structural warm start, 191 random edits on ten Netlib models at `e0b1a68` (`structural-warm-start-e0b1a68.csv`): 103 optimal pairs, 669 warm dual-simplex pivots against 5,689 cold, **0.118x**, fewer on 101; largest relative objective gap 1.25e-14.
- OpenMP gate, the default against `omp_min_work=0` in one job (`option-ab-{netlib,miplib,pooling}-omp-gate-0c9355f.csv`, `option-ab-cycle-ipm-omp-gate-50bfe65.csv`): Netlib full and MIPLIB tier 1 give the same verdicts in both arms, the pooling set passes 32 of 39 in both, and `cycle` under the interior point at 4 threads takes 110.4 s with the gate against 132.2 s without (geometric mean of two repeats).

## Limits, stated

- Convex QCQP is the weak spot: the conic engine reaches `optimal`, but only 1 of 13 QPLIB answers passes the verifier and the 1e-6 match. A KKT gate on the reported duals (#1149) was not merged in time for this candidate.
- On Maros-Meszaros PIQP matches and verifies more QPs than SANKHYA and is about twice as fast by shifted geometric mean.
- Decomposition does not beat the monolithic solve on any measured instance; it is opt-in.
- MIPLIB is as in rc2: on the harder MIPLIB 2017 instances most runs end with a verified feasible point and no proof.
- One wheel per platform, Linux x86-64 and Windows x64 only; no macOS, no aarch64, nothing on PyPI.

The full evidence, including what does not work yet, is in `README.md`, `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` and `docs/NEGATIVE-RESULTS.md` at the tagged commit.
